paraphrase: Comparison and omission bundle. (1) For every profile, thought interpretation and world, whole-carrier well-foundedness of grounding implies thinker-local accessibility, and 'every actual contingent concretum has an actual concrete ground' implies the thinker-local anti-brute-root principle. (2) One finite model (two worlds, universal accessibility; a thinker existing at both worlds, and two mutually grounding concreta and one ungrounded concretum existing only at world true, the selected w) satisfies all six non-logical premises of the necessary-ancestor theorem and its conclusion, so they are jointly satisfiable; its thinker exists at every accessible world and is not contingent; and it falsifies both global premises. (3) Six omission models: dropping occurrence, the bearer principle, bearer concreteness, bearer existence at w, thinker-local accessibility (a two-cycle through a contingent thinker) or the thinker-local anti-brute-root principle (a contingent ungrounded thinker) each keeps the other five true and falsifies the necessary-ancestor conclusion. Logical models only; none is claimed metaphysically possible.
